title: From the Super 6 to the Super Gemini
intro: UDO Audio is a British company, and the Super Gemini is its flagship. It takes the voice of the Super 6, a digital super-wave oscillator and a second oscillator feeding analogue filters on a stereo signal path, and doubles it: two complete layers, upper and lower, each with its own full row of controls, played alone, stacked or split. Its panel was designed with Axel Hartmann.

timeline.name: Roland JP-8000
timeline.text: Its Super Saw put seven detuned sawtooths in one oscillator and became the sound of trance. DDS 1’s super core, a centre oscillator and six sisters spread apart, is the same idea built into a hybrid voice.

timeline.name: UDO Audio Super 6
timeline.text: A twelve-voice binaural analogue-hybrid polysynth: FPGA oscillators, a true-stereo analogue signal path and one layer of controls. The Super Gemini’s two layers are each a Super 6-style voice.

timeline.name: UDO Audio Super Gemini
timeline.text: Twenty voices in two layers, each with DDS 1 and DDS 2, a 6 dB high-pass into a 24 dB low-pass with drive, a VCA, two envelopes with hold stages, LFO 1, chorus and delay, played in SINGLE, DUAL or SPLIT, with a performance LFO, a ribbon, polyphonic aftertouch, a modulation matrix, an arpeggiator and a sequencer. To the Super 6’s engine it adds wave morphing, a ring modulator, a sine sub-oscillator and a delay send.

relatives.name: Yamaha CS-80
relatives.text: Another instrument whose every key can play two complete voices at once, with a ribbon above the keys and a pressure-sensitive keyboard. This app plays it.

relatives.name: Roland Jupiter-8
relatives.text: An eight-voice analogue poly that holds two patches and plays them split or layered across its keyboard. This app plays it.

relatives.name: Oberheim OB-X8
relatives.text: A modern analogue flagship that also plays two sounds split or stacked on its keyboard.
